strengths: Addresses an important and highly relevant problem: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) specifically designed for Vision-Language Object Detectors (VLODs), which has been mostly unexplored compared to classification TTA.

The proposed IoU-weighted Entropy Minimization (IWE) is a clever, spatially aware solution. It effectively leverages the dense, redundant proposals generated by modern detectors to mitigate confirmation bias on isolated/mislocalized false positives.

Demonstrates that standard prompt averaging (which is common in vision-language classification) can actually degrade VLOD performance, and introduces a simple and effective alternative: Image-conditioned Prompt Selection (IPS).

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across diverse distribution shifts (artistic styles, autonomous driving, low light, and synthetic corruptions) using two state-of-the-art and structurally different VLODs (YOLO-World and Grounding DINO).
Excellent ablation studies and sensitivity analysis in the main text and appendix, including explorations of batch size, number of augmentations, adapter placement, and pre-adaptation fine-tuning.
weaknesses: Significant computational overhead: The test-time backward pass and the IoU graph construction drop the throughput of YOLO-World from 89 FPS (zero-shot) to 20 FPS. While this is typical for TTA methods, it significantly limits its applicability for real-time edge applications.

Limitations on small, sparse, or isolated objects: As noted by the authors, when scenes are dominated by tiny, non-overlapping objects (like in some Cityscapes samples), the density-based IoU weight drops, reducing the effectiveness of IWE. The performance on Cityscapes/BDD100K shows much smaller relative gains than on style-shifted datasets.

Hyperparameter sensitivity and tuning: The framework introduces multiple critical hyperparameters ($M$, $\theta$, $\gamma$, $\lambda$, $\rho$). Since TTA assumes no labeled validation set is available at test-time, setting these parameters optimally for a completely unseen domain is challenging and may limit the plug-and-play nature of the method.

strengths: Pioneering work: The paper addresses a highly practical and unexplored problem by introducing the first dedicated test-time adaptation (TTA) framework for Vision-Language Object Detectors (VLODs).

Intuitively motivated components: The proposed IoU-Weighted Entropy (IWE) minimization elegantly exploits the spatial redundancy of dense object proposals to address confirmation bias. Similarly, the Image-conditioned Prompt Selection (IPS) dynamically discards irrelevant prompts on a per-image basis, solving the performance degradation issue associated with standard prompt averaging.

Rigorous evaluation: The method is benchmarked extensively across 6 datasets with diverse domain shifts (style, weather, low-light, driving scenes) plus synthetic corruptions (PASCAL-C and COCO-C). Evaluation is carried out on both CNN-based (YOLO-World) and Transformer-based (Grounding DINO) architectures, demonstrating consistent improvements over zero-shot and classification-adapted TTA baselines.

Clarity and completeness: The manuscript is well-written, with clear motivational figures and a detailed appendix containing comprehensive parameter sensitivity analyses, runtime overhead reports, and extensive qualitative examples.
weaknesses: Heuristic hyperparameter dependency: The framework introduces multiple hyperparameters (IoU threshold $\theta$, cluster exponent $\gamma$, prompt selection fraction $\rho$, and fusion coefficient $\lambda$). Sensitivity analysis shows that optimal values (especially $\theta$ and $\lambda$) vary depending on the dataset. In a realistic, unsupervised TTA setting, tuning these parameters without access to target domain labels is challenging and compromises usability.

Significant computational overhead: Performing backpropagation at test-time to update the adapters and constructing the class-wise IoU graphs leads to a major drop in throughput. On YOLO-World, the frame rate drops from 89 FPS (zero-shot) to 20 FPS. This substantial latency increase could limit the applicability of the method in real-time systems, such as autonomous driving.

Risk of suppressing small/sparse objects: The IWE heavily relies on spatial consensus, assigning lower weights to smaller, isolated proposal clusters. In scenarios containing tiny or sparse objects (such as distant pedestrians or vehicles in Cityscapes/BDD100K), correct proposals may not form large clusters and could be mistakenly suppressed as false positives.

Incremental aspect of the prompt residual tuning: The text-side learnable residual vector $\Delta$ is heavily inspired by existing VLM classification-TTA methods (e.g., DPE), which somewhat limits the novelty of the prompt adaptation mechanism.

strengths: Pioneering Work in VLOD TTA: The paper is one of the first to systematically study test-time adaptation for vision-language object detectors (VLODs), successfully bridging the gap between classification-oriented VLM TTA and detection.

Spatially Aware Objective: The proposed IoU-weighted entropy minimization (IWE) elegantly utilizes the spatial distribution and clustering of dense region proposals to weight their entropy, successfully reducing the typical confirmation bias of standard entropy minimization.

Image-Conditioned Prompt Selection: Introducing image-conditioned prompt selection (IPS) rather than uniform prompt averaging is a well-reasoned and empirically supported design choice, as uniform averaging often dilutes class-specific visual features in dense detection.

Rigorous and Extensive Evaluation: The benchmarking is exceptionally thorough, spanning two popular architectures (YOLO-World and Grounding DINO) across 6 mainstream datasets and 15 corruptions, encompassing a total of 96 distinct test scenarios.

High-Quality Ablations and Analysis: The paper features deep ablation studies, including adapter placement, prompt generation sources, hyperparameter sensitivity, batch sizes, and a very informative qualitative visualization of proposal clusters.
weaknesses: Modest Gains over Adapter Baseline in Certain Settings: In some challenging scenarios, such as Cityscapes and ExDark, the performance improvement of VLOD-TTA over the standard Adapter baseline (which uses TENT-like entropy) is quite marginal (e.g., +0.3 mAP on Cityscapes, +0.6 mAP on ExDark for YOLO-World).

Scalability to On-the-Fly Open-Vocabulary Queries: Since VLODs are designed for open-vocabulary detection, a user might input arbitrary text queries during inference. VLOD-TTA relies on a pre-generated pool of GPT prompts (T=16) per class. The authors should discuss how the method scales when a completely novel class query is introduced on-the-fly (e.g., whether it can fall back to standard templates without access to GPT).

Computational Overhead of Graph Construction: Constructing the IoU graph and finding connected components over M=600 proposals adds test-time CPU/GPU overhead. Although the throughput (Table 3) only drops from 22 FPS to 20 FPS on YOLO-World, a detailed runtime breakdown of the graph clustering vs. the backward pass would help assess the scalability to devices with weaker processors.

Hyperparameter Sensitivity: The performance of the IWE and IPS components is sensitive to several hyperparameters (θ, γ, λ, ρ). Figure 6 reveals that the optimal IoU threshold (θ) and prompt-selection ratio (ρ) vary depending on the dataset characteristics (e.g., average object size). In a true test-time scenario where the target domain is unknown, tuning these hyperparameters dynamically remains a challenge.

strengths: The paper addresses a highly practical and under-explored topic: test-time adaptation (TTA) specifically designed for vision-language object detectors (VLODs).

The proposed IoU-weighted entropy minimization (IWE) is a technically sound and elegant way to leverage spatial redundancy in object detection to mitigate confirmation bias, which is a key limitation of standard entropy minimization in detection tasks.

The image-conditioned prompt selection (IPS) module introduces a dynamic way to choose contextually relevant prompts per image instead of using simple prompt averaging, which can often degrade detection performance.
The method demonstrates strong efficiency, requiring far fewer parameters and significantly lower latency compared to the teacher-student-based prior state-of-the-art method (TTAOD-F).

Extensive experiments across 6 datasets and various corruptions (PASCAL-C, COCO-C) demonstrate the robust performance and generalization capabilities of the proposed method across both CNN-based (YOLO-World) and transformer-based (Grounding DINO) architectures.
The ablation studies and supplementary materials are exceptionally comprehensive, covering hyperparameter sensitivity, failure cases (e.g., on Cityscapes), and performance on specialized domains.
weaknesses: The method introduces several hyperparameters (such as $\theta$ for IoU thresholding, $\gamma$ for cluster size weighting, and $\lambda$ for prompt fusion) which might require some manual adjustment depending on the target domain, although the authors provide a helpful sensitivity analysis showing reasonable stability.

As noted by the authors, IWE is less effective on scenes with many small, non-overlapping objects (like Cityscapes) because reliable proposal clusters do not form well at lower resolutions, though using higher-resolution inputs can partially mitigate this.

strengths: The paper addresses a highly practical and relatively unexplored problem: test-time adaptation (TTA) specifically designed for vision-language object detectors (VLODs), which is crucial for deploying open-vocabulary detectors in changing environments.

The proposed IoU-weighted entropy (IWE) minimization is a clever, detector-specific design that leverages spatial redundancy (overlapping proposals) to mitigate confirmation bias on isolated false positives, showing a clear advantage over standard independent proposal entropy minimization.
The image-conditioned prompt selection (IPS) successfully mitigates the negative effect of uniform prompt averaging in VLODs, retaining only image-compatible text prompts to enhance performance.

Extensive experimental results across multiple challenging datasets (Watercolor, ClipArt, Comic, Cityscapes, BDD100K, ExDark, PASCAL-C, COCO-C) and two different VLOD architectures (CNN-based YOLO-World and Transformer-based Grounding DINO) demonstrate consistent improvements.
VLOD-TTA offers a significantly better accuracy-efficiency trade-off than the prior state-of-the-art (TTAOD-F), using much less GPU memory (3.76 GB vs 11.37 GB) and maintaining lower latency.
weaknesses: The core assumption of IWE relies on dense proposal overlap. As analyzed in the failure case section for Cityscapes, the method's performance degrades in scenes dominated by small or non-overlapping objects, as well as classes with high semantic overlap (e.g., rider vs. person).

The method introduces several hyperparameters (e.g., θ, ​γ, M, λ, ρ). While sensitivity analysis is provided, some parameters like the IoU threshold θ show some dataset-dependence (peaking at 0.7 for Watercolor but 0.5 for ClipArt/Comic), which might limit its completely robust out-of-the-box performance without target-specific tuning.

Although much faster than TTAOD-F, the necessity of a backward pass per image still significantly reduces throughput compared to the zero-shot baseline (from 89 FPS down to 20 FPS on YOLO-World), which may limit its application in extremely latency-sensitive real-time edge environments.

strengths: Addresses an important and relatively unexplored area: online test-time adaptation (TTA) specifically designed for open-vocabulary Vision-Language Object Detectors (VLODs).

Introduces two technically sound and well-motivated components: IoU-weighted entropy minimization (IWE) to combat confirmation bias by leveraging local proposal overlap, and image-conditioned prompt selection (IPS) to select context-relevant prompt templates dynamically.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Watercolor, ClipArt, Comic, Cityscapes, BDD100K, ExDark, PASCAL-C, COCO-C) using state-of-the-art CNN-based (YOLO-World) and transformer-based (Grounding DINO) VLODs.

Demonstrates excellent efficiency improvements over the prior state-of-the-art VLOD-TTA method (TTAOD-F), significantly reducing parameter count, GPU memory usage, and inference latency while achieving comparable or superior accuracy.
The manuscript is clearly written and provides highly detailed ablation studies, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, and failure-case investigations (e.g., on Cityscapes).
weaknesses: The method still requires backpropagation at test-time, which significantly reduces the inference throughput (e.g., YOLO-World FPS drops from 89 to 20), limiting its feasibility for real-time edge deployment.
Performance gains on more structured driving scenes (e.g., Cityscapes and BDD100K) are relatively modest compared to stylized datasets, due to the high frequency of small objects and label overlap.

The construction of the IoU-weighted entropy objective introduces several hyperparameters (such as the IoU threshold $\theta$ and exponent $\gamma$) which, although stable, show some dataset dependence for achieving optimal performance.
